No. The decision in native-spec-and-okn.md records an accepted runtime boundary ("Use `openknowledge-sh/openknowledge`'s `okn` as the canonical broader KNOW implementation"), but an accepted decision is not proof of current behavior, and decisions.md says so explicitly. The dated 2026-09-05 observation supersedes it for the inspected code: `search()` already delegates to `pkstack.knowledge_acp.search`, and the former `okn search` implementation survives only as `_legacy_search`, which `search()` does not call. So the public knowledge search, as inspected, does not invoke `okn`.

Search and validation diverge. Validation still prefers the `okn` subprocess and reports `mode: "canonical-okn"` when the executable is present, with the local-only path labeled degraded; the observation calls that unfinished migration work rather than a retained optional backend (the spec rejects an optional `okn` backend). So the canonical-okn boundary still describes validation behavior while search has moved to ACP.

Runtime proof is absent either way. The observation is source inspection with no command executed, and `pkstack.knowledge_acp` was not read, so nothing establishes how the ACP search actually behaves at runtime. The budget bounds, `okf+sha256://` locator checks, and `work/` exclusion belong to the dead `okn` adapter and are explicitly not attributed to the active ACP search.
